questions.question: When traveling downhill, your vehicle will:

options.text: Travel at the same speed as on flat road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: Gravity makes your vehicle go faster downhill. Slow down before you reach a downgrade.

questions.question: When driving doubles, the shut-off valves at the rear of the first trailer should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: When driving doubles or triples, close the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer only. Keep all other shut-off valves open.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you should not:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drain the brake fluid.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your engine, check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level. Do not drain brake fluid.

questions.question: Black ice is:

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road.
A thin layer of ice on the road.
Ice that looks black because of road debris.

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. It looks like a wet road. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Press the brake pedal down quickly.
Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly.
Lift the brake pedal up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal down in a smooth, gradual motion.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Usually happens only when traveling faster than 65 mph.
Can happen even with a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen even with a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your tires lose grip and slide on a layer of water. It does not require a large amount of water to happen.

questions.question: If a vehicle's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working:

options.text: The vehicle will have no brakes.
The vehicle will still have brakes.
The vehicle will likely go faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: ABS helps prevent wheel lockup by reducing brake pressure. If ABS fails, your basic brakes still work. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you better control when braking.
Slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even if ABS is on only the tractor, trailer, or one axle, you still have more braking control than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: Shaded areas of a road:

options.text: Are protected from moisture and cannot freeze.
Stay slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and warm up more slowly. They stay icy and slippery after ice has melted elsewhere on the road.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of bad brakes?

options.text: Pads that are clean and dry
Shoes with oil or grease on them
Shoes that are worn too thin

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads that are clean and dry
questions.explanation: When checking brakes, look for cracked drums, pads or shoes covered in oil, grease, or brake fluid, and pads or shoes that are missing, broken, or too thin.

questions.question: You are most likely to encounter strong winds when:
questions.correctAnswerText: Exiting a tunnel.
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. This is especially dangerous when you exit a tunnel.

questions.question: ____ is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road.
questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is clear ice that lets you see the road through it. A road with black ice looks wet instead of icy. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet and the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: Watching the road ahead helps you:

options.text: Plan how to avoid a hazard before you reach it.
Stay focused, unlike other driving tasks.
Drive safely only in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to avoid a hazard before you reach it.
questions.explanation: Always watch for hazards ahead. This gives you time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: Do not shift gears based on:

options.text: What other vehicles next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What other vehicles next to you are doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range or your vehicle's speed. Do not base this decision on other vehicles around you.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning light:

options.text: Should not be used on vehicles with air brakes.
Must be on all vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be on all vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: Every vehicle with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning light.

questions.question: Before you enter a curve, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift.
questions.explanation: You must downshift before entering a curve to help maintain control.

questions.question: Within 10 minutes of stopping on the roadside, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Set up emergency warning devices.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the roadside, place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes.

questions.question: ABS helps you:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control while braking.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up during hard braking. Drive and brake the same way with or without ABS.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, like at dawn or dusk, you can make your vehicle more visible by:

options.text: Flashing your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights at dawn, dusk, and in bad weather to make your vehicle more visible.

questions.question: When checking a mirror, you should:

options.text: Use only your driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a quick glance.
questions.explanation: Look at mirrors quickly. If you stare at a mirror too long, you will miss what is ahead of you on the road.
